To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TG2 catalyzed the incorporation of the donor biotinylated glutamine peptide into the N-terminus and C-terminus of human OPN and that TG2-mediated cross-linking of OPN required both Gln and Lyc residues located in the C-terminus.

the N-terminal part and the C-terminal part are the major reactive sites for TG2-mediated modification and polymerization of OPN, and that the location of reactive glutamine and lysin residues in the C-terminal part is important for the polymerization of full-length OPN
the transglutaminases (TGs) can catalyse polymerization of OPN by cross-linking of the glutamines and lysines in the N- and the C-terminal parts of the protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the reactive residues in OPN that are important for the polymerization of this protein by the enzyme transglutamine 2.
the identification of the transglutaminases reactive residues in human osteopontin (hOPN), and the elucidation of the importance of these residues for polymerization of hOPN.
the role of posttranslational modifications of the bone matrix protein Osteopontinin (OPN) in its interaction with integrins and the subsequent activation of the cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OPN can be crosslinked in the C-terminal part by TG2, but that full-length OPN is unable to polymerize in the presence of TG2.
the N-terminal part is the most important part in OPN for its biological activity and that the C-terminal part is important for the polymerization.
OPN is a substrate of TG2, and that the distribution of the reactive Gln and the presence of the Lys residues in the C-terminal part are essential for OPN polymerization to occur.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal part is the major site for TG2-mediated polymerization of OPN, and that the N-terminal part is not involved in polymerization.
OPN polymerization is a multistep process, in which the N-terminal part is the first to be modified, followed by the C-terminal part.

TG2-mediated polymerization of OPN is a complex process involving multiple reactive Gln and/or Lys residues in the C-terminal part as well as the full-length molecule, and that the polymerization is important for the biological activity of this multifunctional protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TG2-mediated polymerization of OPN requires a specific distribution of reactive residues and that this polymerization is not a simple consequence of TG2 catalysis.
TG2 catalyzes the incorporation of the donor peptide biotin-TVQQEL-OEt at Gln34, 42, 193 and 248 in OPN.
the distribution and reactivity of Gln and LK residues in OPN are important for polymerization.
